learning_objective: 🎯 Master the ratios of sides in a right-angled triangle, understand specific angle values, and learn to prove trigonometric identities!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: In a right triangle, the ratios are: sin = Perpendicular/Hypotenuse, cos = Base/Hypotenuse, tan = Perpendicular/Base. (A popular trick to remember: 'Pandit Badri Prasad, Har Har Bhole').
The other three ratios are just flips of the first three: cosec is 1/sin, sec is 1/cos, and cot is 1/tan.
You must memorize the values of sin, cos, and tan for standard angles: 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, and 90°. (e.g., sin 30° = 1/2).
Equations involving trig ratios that are true for all angles. The most important fundamental identity is: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1. The others are 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

fun_activity.title: 🏗️ Building a Clinometer
fun_activity.instructions: Tape a straw to a protractor, hang a weight from the center with a string, and look through the straw at a tall tree. The string will show you the exact angle of elevation to use in your trig calculations!

exam_tips: 📌 When proving identities, always start with the more complex side (usually LHS) and try converting all terms into sine and cosine first.
📌 Make a habit of quickly drawing the standard angle value table on the last page of your answer sheet during reading time.
📌 Remember that 'sin A' is a single symbol representing the sine of angle A; it is NOT the product of 'sin' and 'A'.
quick_recap: ⭐ The value of sin θ and cos θ never exceeds 1.
⭐ tan θ = sin θ / cos θ and cot θ = cos θ / sin θ.
⭐ Trigonometry literally means measuring the sides of a triangle (tri-gon-metry).
